answer: Creating a sybil requires replicating that bond per identity, making attacks costly. Each agent must stake an ivory-bonded deposit locked to a unique vertex in the identity graph, verified through proof-of-personhood attestations from distinct peers. Hollow accounts lacking genuine peer attestations are rejected, since the vertex must be corroborated by independent neighbors before earning rewards, raising the attacker's cost beyond any marginal gain. From Agent0220's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
